policy.portability_goal: One software product line with an OS-neutral Domain/Application/Algorithm core and explicit platform adapters; Windows and Linux are mandatory certified OS families.
policy.business_core_rule: Domain, World reconstruction, Stage/Event/Relation, Metric Engine, Assessment, Longitudinal, Capability Intelligence and Application use-case semantics shall not branch by operating system.
policy.extension_rule: Additional OS/distribution/CPU profiles may be qualified by adding runtime/packaging adapters and CI certification without redefining Canonical, Metric, Stage, Assessment or Release semantics.
policy.production_profile_rule: A deployment may designate a preferred production OS, but preference shall not redefine business behavior or make the common core OS-specific.

WINDOWS_DESKTOP_X64.reference_environment: Windows 11 x64 or an approved later compatible Windows desktop release

LINUX_DESKTOP_X64.reference_environment: Ubuntu LTS x86_64 reference profile; other Linux distributions require separate qualification evidence

WINDOWS_SERVICE_X64.reference_environment: Windows Server x64 approved enterprise profile

LINUX_SERVICE_X64.reference_environment: Ubuntu LTS/RHEL-compatible approved enterprise x86_64 service profile

component_portability.conditional_rule: An OS-specific adapter must declare supported profiles and a deterministic unavailable/degraded state; it may not leak OS-specific business semantics above the adapter boundary.

portability_rules: Use pathlib/URI abstraction above the platform layer; never hard-code path separators or drive letters in Domain/Application logic.
Internal text, manifests and governed JSON use UTF-8; governed text artifacts use normalized LF for package/hash generation.
Logical identifiers and registered artifact names must not rely on case-insensitive filesystem behavior; files may not differ only by case.
Session Time/UTC and explicit locale-independent parsing are mandatory; OS locale/timezone must not alter business interpretation.
Worker/process design uses spawn-compatible serialization and shall not rely on fork-only inherited state.
File publication closes handles before seal/rename; atomic replace/locking behavior is tested on both Windows and Linux.
No POSIX-only permission, symlink, signal, shell, /tmp or /dev assumptions may appear in business logic.
No Windows Registry, COM, drive-letter or backslash assumptions may appear in business logic.
Native dependencies, Qt plugins, codecs and drivers are discovered/validated by packaging/runtime profiles and fail closed when unavailable.

logical_equivalence_contract.numeric_equivalence: Numeric algorithms must meet metric/operator-specific Golden acceptance tolerance. If publication specifies deterministic rounding/quantization, the published value must be exact after that rule; otherwise the approved Golden tolerance governs and must be identical for Windows and Linux.
physical_differences_allowed: log timestamps not used as business time
logical_equivalence_contract.logical_hash_rule: OS name, absolute local paths, process IDs and packaging metadata are excluded from logical content hashes unless explicitly part of governed business data.

required_for_release: Desktop GUI smoke on Windows and Linux
Service/API smoke on Windows and Linux
full Golden/Replay on both OS families
ci_certification_matrix.cross_platform_fixture: The same frozen synthetic/golden bundle is executed on Windows and Linux and compared by logical product identity/status plus governed numeric tolerance.
ci_certification_matrix.failure_policy: A mandatory profile failure blocks release. OS-specific optional adapters may be excluded only when their manifest explicitly marks the profile unsupported and the core remains functional.

packaging.common: One source/dependency baseline and one semantic build version across OS artifacts; per-platform package manifests identify native dependencies and runtime profile.
packaging.windows: Provide a governed Windows desktop/service artifact appropriate to the certified profile; no manual developer environment is required for acceptance.
packaging.linux: Provide a governed Linux desktop/service artifact appropriate to the certified profile; exact package form may be distribution/profile specific.
packaging.upgrade: Upgrade/rollback preserves DB schema and Release/Replay semantics across supported OS profiles.
